turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: Our khashaa in the ger district, on the north side of Ulaanbaatar, Bayankhoshuu. This is about 2005. A khashaa is the fenced yard. High wooden fence, planks, all the way around, and the ger inside it. Not in the middle, more toward the back.

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: A metal gate in the fence, on the south side, the street side, painted blue. There was always a dog chained by the gate, Khasar, he barked at everyone. You walk in, the ger is ahead of you, and a little wooden house, a baishin, to the left. My uncle built it, but we only used it for storage, in winter it was too cold to live in.

turns.speaker: B
turns.transcript: And the ger itself, the door?

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: The door faces south, always, every ger does. Wooden, painted orange, low, you have to duck. And you must not step on the threshold, my grandmother would hit you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: The stove in the centre, the zuukh, iron, with the pipe going straight up through the toono, the crown, the round wooden ring at the top. Two orange posts, the bagana, holding up the toono, one each side of the stove.

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: Beds around the wall. My grandparents' bed was on the left side. No, wait. As you come in, the left is west, that's the men's side, where the saddle was and my grandfather's things. Their bed was on the right, the east side, toward the back. Me and my sister had a low bed on the left, by the door.

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: The khoimor, the back, across from the door, the place of honour. There was a painted chest there, orange and blue, with a little Buddha and the family photos on top, and the TV on a small table beside it. Guests always sat at the back.

turns.speaker: A
turns.transcript: Five walls, five khana, the lattice sections, so maybe six metres across. Oh, and the outhouse, I should say, a wooden toilet in the far corner of the khashaa, the back left. A hole in the ground. Minus thirty in January. You were quick.
